question: How do these people see and do things, from the inside?

goodson2011.cite: Goodson & Vassar (2011). An overview of ethnography in healthcare and medical education research. Journal of Educational Evaluation for Health Professions 8: 4.
goodson2011.checked: every quote read word for word in the Europe PMC full text (PMC3100516) on 20 Nov 2026; the article is short and online, so places are its section headings; in-text reference numbers are left out of the quotes

steps.title: Get in
steps.text: Prepare, then win access to the group. A trusted member, a key informant, opens doors an outsider cannot.

quotes.text: they must be accepted temporarily within the culture in order to gather accurate information.
Additionally, the development of key informants is essential.

steps.title: Observe and take part
steps.text: Live and work alongside the people you study, in their own setting, and write field notes on what you see and hear. Interviews add their own words.

quotes.text: Ethnographies are normally conducted in a single setting, and data collection is largely dependent upon participant observation and interviews.

steps.title: Stay long
steps.text: Stay for months, not days. Only long exposure lets you describe the setting richly and see past the show put on for a visitor.

quotes.text: ethnography is a research method characterized by long-term fieldwork since thick description of the participants and setting may only be acquired from sufficient exposure to them.

steps.title: Follow the leads
steps.text: Let the field change the plan. A conversation raises a question you did not expect, and you go after it.

quotes.text: In ethnography, data collection can sometimes change along the course of the study. A conversation with one study participant may lead to generation of further questions.
quotes.where: “Uses of ethnography”, the Perry et al. example

steps.title: Interpret through culture
steps.text: Read your notes through the group's own culture and history, and write an account that its members would recognise.

quotes.text: presenting an accurate reflection of participant perspectives and behaviors
quotes.where: “Introduction”, characteristic 3 of LeCompte and Schensul's seven

quotes.text: using the concept of culture as a lens through which to interpret study results

researcher-lens.text: Subjectivity is certainly a limitation of ethnography. The interpretation of the cultural experience will vary among researchers.

external-validity.text: It is difficult to generalize with the ethnography method.

limits: The card's reference, Reeves et al. (2008) in the BMJ, is not open access and was not read; the page quotes Goodson & Vassar (2011), an introductory overview that itself synthesises other authors (Leung, Savage, LeCompte and Schensul, Pope, Atkinson and Pugsley).
Whyte's and Latour & Woolgar's books, the card's examples, were not read for this page.
The step texts in our own words are summaries of the quotes beside them; the quotes are the authority.
